annotation_description: In a 4-player Commander game, choosing to go first means you draw fewer cards (no draw on your first turn) and become the first visible threat. With a hand that has no 1-drop or 2-drop creature (only lands, Blackblade Reforged, Military Intelligence, and expensive spells like Notorious Throng and Soul Manipulation), there's little benefit to going first. The hand wants to set up with lands and hold up interaction, which benefits more from drawing extra cards and acting later.

Mossfire Valley requires {1} plus tapping to produce mana, so playing it as your only land on turn 1 means you have zero available mana. Forest would give {G} immediately. While there's nothing castable in hand for 1 mana, having mana available is strictly better, and both sequencings produce the same mana on turn 2.

Playing Swamp is redundant with Vivid Marsh's black mana production. The hand is heavily white-demanding (Hour of Reckoning, Teneb, Karador all need white) and they have no white source yet without spending a Vivid Marsh charge counter.

Playing Orzhov Basilica on turn 3 instead of Plains means bouncing a land back to hand, resulting in only 2 mana available this turn (and the Basilica enters tapped). Playing Plains would give 3 mana available immediately (Plains + Vivid Marsh + Swamp), allowing a turn 3 play like Acorn Catapult. With the Basilica, the bounced land needs to be replayed next turn, effectively setting back mana development by a turn. The Basilica does provide mana fixing and virtual card advantage long-term, but playing Plains first and Basilica later (when there are more lands to bounce without losing tempo) would be better sequencing. Playing Plains now gives 3 mana for Acorn Catapult, then Basilica next turn bouncing a basic still yields 4 mana on turn 4.

Karador, Ghost Chieftain gets cheaper to cast for each creature card in the graveyard, so discarding it loses access to a potentially powerful commander-cost-reduction creature. However, with only 2 lands in play and a hand full of expensive cards, Gem3F ESPN needed to keep lands and more castable cards. The real question is whether discarding Cobra Trap (which is situational and hard to cast at 6 mana without the trap condition) or Acorn Catapult (a weak artifact) would have been better. Karador at 8 CMC is very expensive but has built-in cost reduction and can be cast from graveyard-style effects. Cobra Trap is extremely situational and unlikely to be cast for its trap cost, making it arguably the better discard.

Playing Myriad Landscape instead of an untapped basic land means Gem25F Analyst has less mana available this turn and next turn (since Myriad Landscape enters tapped). With 5 lands on board (3 untapped after this play), they have no meaningful plays this turn anyway with their hand of expensive spells. However, playing an untapped basic (Island or Swamp) would give them 4 available mana, which still isn't enough for their spells but keeps them more flexible for holding up Soul Manipulation (1UB = 3 mana, which they could do with either land drop). With Myriad Landscape entering tapped, they only have 3 available mana sources (2 Islands + 1 Swamp), which is exactly enough for Soul Manipulation. But playing Island would give them 3 Islands + 1 Swamp = 4 mana, still enough for Soul Manipulation with mana to spare. The Myriad Landscape is better played later when you can sacrifice it immediately or when the tempo loss matters less. Playing Island now keeps the option to play Myriad Landscape later while having more mana available. That said, the ramp from Myriad Landscape is valuable long-term, and playing it early maximizes the chance of having mana to activate it. This is close but slightly suboptimal sequencing.

Gem3F ESPN played Swamp when they already had two black sources (Vivid Marsh and Orzhov Basilica) but only one white source (Orzhov Basilica). Their hand contains Hour of Reckoning (4WWW) and Teneb the Harvester (3WBG), both requiring white mana. Playing Plains would better fix their mana for upcoming turns.

Berserker's Frenzy is an instant that can only be cast before combat or during combat before blockers are declared. On turn 4 with no attackers and no meaningful combat scenario, casting it accomplishes virtually nothing - it forces creatures to block or lets you choose blockers, but there's no combat happening where this matters. The player's own reasoning trail shows they realized the Hydra at X=0 would die immediately, but then defaulted to casting Berserker's Frenzy which is equally wasteful. With only 3 lands and a hand full of expensive threats, wasting a card and 3 mana on a spell with no meaningful impact is a real mistake.

Discarding Magmaquake over Berserker's Frenzy is debatable. Magmaquake is a flexible board wipe that scales with mana and hits all non-flying creatures and planeswalkers - very relevant in a multiplayer game where tokens and ground creatures are common. Berserker's Frenzy is a narrow combat trick that requires specific dice rolls to be effective. In a multiplayer game with token generators like Acorn Catapult already on board, Magmaquake's sweeper potential seems more valuable than a conditional combat trick.

Notorious Throng creates X tokens where X is the damage dealt to opponents this turn. Cast in precombat main with no prior damage dealt this turn, X=0, so it creates zero tokens. It's essentially a 4-mana spell that does nothing. The Prowl cost wasn't paid either (no Rogue combat damage), so no extra turn. This wastes a card and 4 mana for zero effect.

Sonnet Valley has 5 lands including Opal Palace, Caves of Koilos, Bojuka Bog, Victory Chimes, and wants to cast Fain, the Broker (2B). By tapping Opal Palace for just colorless mana instead of using its second ability ({1}, {T}: Add one mana of any color in commander's color identity), they miss the opportunity to use Opal Palace's color-fixing ability. While Fain costs {2}{B} and they could get black from Caves of Koilos, using Opal Palace's second ability would preserve life (Caves deals 1 damage) or provide flexibility. More importantly, the reasoning text shows confusion and the player seems to be fumbling with the interface rather than making a deliberate mana decision. However, this is a relatively small optimization since they can still cast Fain using Caves of Koilos for the black mana.

Casting Syphon Flesh with only 5 mana available (Vivid Marsh, Orzhov Basilica, Swamp, Forest, and the Forest that needs to tap) costs 4B. The player has exactly 5 mana to cast it. However, this is turn 5 and the player hasn't played their land for the turn yet (Plains is in hand). They should play Plains first before casting spells. More importantly, Harmonize would be a much better play here - it draws 3 cards for 2GG, helping find more lands and develop. Syphon Flesh forces each opponent to sacrifice a creature, but looking at the board: Haiku Gramps has no creatures, Sonnet Valley has only Fain, the Broker, and Gem25F Analyst has no creatures. So Syphon Flesh will only get 1 sacrifice (from Sonnet Valley) and create only 1 Zombie token, which is poor value for a 5-mana spell. Harmonize drawing 3 cards is significantly better when only one opponent even has a creature to sacrifice.

Should play Plains from hand before casting Harmonize. Playing the land first costs nothing and leaves an additional mana available after Harmonize resolves, which could matter if one of the 3 drawn cards is a 1-mana spell or if they want to activate Acorn Catapult. Always play lands before spells when there's no reason to hold them.

Failed to activate Acorn Catapult with available mana during postcombat main. Could have pinged themselves for 1 damage to create a 1/1 Squirrel token, which would help with future Hour of Reckoning convoke and provide board presence at minimal cost (1 mana + 1 life).

Casting Murder on Fain, the Broker is a questionable use of premium removal in a 4-player game. Fain is a 3/3 that requires mana and sacrifices to generate value, and Sonnet Valley only has 4 lands with limited mana available. More importantly, Murder is cast as a sorcery-speed play during the precombat main phase, giving up the ability to hold it as instant-speed interaction for a more threatening target later. The player should be developing their own board with Whirler Rogue (which creates two Thopter tokens, synergizes with Military Intelligence for card draw when attacking with 2+ creatures, and can make creatures unblockable with Anowon's mill/draw strategy). Spending Murder proactively on a modest threat while forgoing board development that enables the deck's card advantage engine is a significant misallocation of resources.

With 6 lands (Vivid Marsh, Orzhov Basilica, Swamp, Forest, Forest, and an unplayed Plains in hand), the player should play the Plains from hand before casting Harmonize. Playing the land first costs nothing and ensures they don't miss a land drop. After casting Harmonize with all 4 mana (2GG from the two Forests plus 2 from Orzhov Basilica/Swamp/Vivid Marsh), they would have no mana left and the Plains would remain unplayed this turn. By playing the Plains first, they'd have 7 lands on board, which matters for future turns and for casting expensive spells like Teneb (6 mana) or Hour of Reckoning (7 mana with convoke).

Vengeful Ancestor (3/4 flying with goad ability) arguably provides more immediate board impact than Chameleon Colossus in a multiplayer game. The goad effect forces opponents to attack each other, which synergizes with Vrondiss's enrage theme (goaded creatures dealing 1 damage to their controller) and provides political advantage. Chameleon Colossus is a strong creature with protection from black and pump ability, but it's a ground creature with no evasion and no immediate board impact beyond being a 4/4. Additionally, casting a creature before combat when holding Berserker's Frenzy (a combat trick) is generally fine since Haiku Gramps has no creatures to attack with yet anyway.

Berserker's Frenzy can only be cast 'before combat or during combat before blockers are declared' and is meant to manipulate blocking. Casting it in precombat main with no attackers and no combat happening accomplishes absolutely nothing - it's a combat trick that requires creatures attacking to have any effect. The card forces creatures to block or lets you choose how creatures block, but there are no attacking creatures to block. This wastes a card and 3 mana for zero effect. The player should have cast Neverwinter Hydra instead, which with X=0 would die immediately but at least with 4 lands (producing RRGG from Mossfire Valley + Forest + Forest + Mountain) they can't cast it for any meaningful X anyway. However, Berserker's Frenzy is still a complete waste - even if cast at the right timing, there are no creatures attacking to make the blocking manipulation relevant on the player's own turn with no creatures on their board.

Casting Gideon, Champion of Justice on turn 7 with only 6 lands and a hand full of expensive threats (Angel of Serenity at 7 mana, Teysa at 7 mana, Necropolis Regent at 6 mana, Sunscorch Regent at 5 mana). Gideon is a relatively weak planeswalker in multiplayer - his +1 is slow, his 0 ability makes him vulnerable as a creature, and his -15 ultimate is extremely unlikely to be reached. Meanwhile, Sunscorch Regent at 5 mana next turn would be a much stronger play providing an evasive body that grows and gains life in multiplayer. Gideon will likely just eat attacks and die without providing meaningful value. Gem25F Analyst played a land before casting Merfolk Windrobber. With Military Intelligence on the battlefield, deploying creatures before combat is important to enable attacking with two creatures to trigger the card draw. However, the more significant issue is sequencing: playing the land first is fine, but they should also cast Merfolk Windrobber in this main phase to have it ready for combat. The real concern is whether they cast the Windrobber at all this turn. Additionally, with Blackblade Reforged on the battlefield and now 6 lands (after playing the Swamp), the equipment could be relevant. The land play itself is correct - making the land drop is important. But casting Merfolk Windrobber before combat would be ideal since it has flying and could deal combat damage to trigger milling, and if they have another creature, Military Intelligence would trigger. Looking at the board, Gem25F Analyst has no creatures on the battlefield, so casting Windrobber pre-combat is correct to at least start building a board presence. This is just a land drop though - they likely plan to cast Windrobber next. This seems like a reasonable sequencing choice (land before spell).

Gem25F Analyst spent 7 mana to equip Blackblade Reforged, but looking at their battlefield, they have no creatures to equip it to. The Whirler Rogue ability mention suggests there may be a Whirler Rogue and Thopters on the board (not fully listed), but equipping Blackblade Reforged for 7 mana is an enormous tempo loss when the board state doesn't warrant it. They have 8 lands so Blackblade would give +8/+8, but spending their entire turn on this instead of developing board presence is questionable at best. More critically, the reasoning text cuts off mid-sentence, suggesting the AI didn't finish evaluating options before choosing. With Merfolk Windrobber available as a cheap play that provides evasive damage, mill synergy with Anowon (their commander likely), and card draw potential, casting the Windrobber and keeping mana open would have been far more efficient. Paying 7 mana to equip when they could instead cast a creature and hold up mana is a massive tempo mistake.

By attacking with only Whirler Rogue, Gem25F Analyst missed the Military Intelligence trigger which requires attacking with 2+ creatures. They could have tapped Blackblade Reforged + 1 Thopter token to make Whirler Rogue unblockable, then attacked with Whirler Rogue + the other Thopter token to trigger Military Intelligence and draw a card.
